report.text: DoD results: (a) fixed -- codex-critic-selected-host.mjs:137 no longer collapses an observed childStarted:false into undefined; it now passes the consumer's boolean through unchanged (typeof result?.childStarted === 'boolean' ? result.childStarted : undefined), so noChild() runs and the receipt records childStarted:false with observed nulled. Traced and confirmed the runSelectedCriticHost code-inversion fix too: the new round-trip test shows it now returns 'selected-sandbox-required' (previously 'selected-critic-transport-failed') when the real bridge observes no child. Red/green proof: added the new tests FIRST against the unfixed source; the surgical test ('selectedCriticInProcessBridge.launch reports a genuinely unstarted child as childStarted:false, not undefined') failed with actual {childStarted: undefined} vs expected {childStarted: false} (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1-red-codex-critic-host-test.txt, exitCode 1); after the fix the same run passed 109/109 (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1-green-codex-critic-host-test.txt, exitCode 0). Did not use git stash/checkout for the revert -- the pre-fix tree IS the red run, satisfying the DoD's revert/red/restore/green sequence without a destructive op. (b) closed at the seam: 'the real runSandboxedReadonlyHostBridge resolves a genuinely unstarted child to noChild()...' drives the REAL runSandboxedReadonlyHostBridge with only readSelection/readback/resolveScratch/resealScratch stubs plus the real selected-Critic launch/finalize pair; the process-spawn boundary (spawnFn/buildSandboxInvocationFn inside the real invokeCodexCriticAppServer) is where the fake sits. A second test performs the same drive underneath a thin executeSandboxedReadonlyDuty stand-in (mirroring that function's own documented no-child translation) to prove runSelectedCriticHost's top-level code too. What remains UNPROVEN: no physical child process anywhere in this suite; createCodexSandboxRuntimeTransport's own composition is not exercised; the store/journal/selectCodexSandbox layer inside the real executeSandboxedReadonlyDuty (durable selection persistence, journal phases) stays undriven -- only its documented no-child translation is reproduced as test glue. (c) resolved -- the advisory-host-bridge.mjs comment is now restated as an explicit open question ('an OPEN QUESTION this file does not answer... Treat it as unconfirmed either way'), not an unbacked claim of fact; not backed with an executable probe since that would mean reading/testing a file outside scope. Existing-case count: 105 before, 105 after, all assertions untouched; 4 new tests added (106-109); full suite 109/109 pass both times (green run). Evidence: node --test plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/codex-critic-host.test.mjs and node --test harness/scripts/check-consumer-safe-paths.test.mjs both captured via capture-evidence.mjs, both exitCode 0 (evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1-green-codex-critic-host-test.txt, evidence/NVA-B-XPORTFIX-1-check-consumer-safe-paths-test.txt). No live Codex execution attempted (out of scope, per briefing). Deliberately not changed: advisory-host-bridge.mjs still carries the identical `false -> undefined` expression at its own mirrored spot -- explicitly out of scope per the briefing's precedent note, left untouched. The completed-but-invalid path's discarded exitCode/signal/stdinEnded observation was NOT changed (postLaunchFailure() still records exitCode:null/stdioStatus:'lost' regardless), per the briefing's explicit prohibition. Opinion on whether it is worth carrying through, as requested: inspected sandboxed-readonly-duty.mjs's schema and bindSandboxedReadonlyDuty gate -- the schema's terminal.exitCode accepts any safe integer (not just 0/null), and bindSandboxedReadonlyDuty independently gates on execution.dutyReceipt.status (not solely on the terminal shape), so carrying the real exitCode/signal through on the completed-but-invalid path would NOT by itself create a binding bypass -- dutyReceipt.status stays 'error' regardless of what terminal fields say. The one real constraint is that terminal.stdioStatus is a closed 3-value enum (complete/lost/not-started) with no distinct 'completed-but-invalid' value, so a true stdio completion would have to be recorded as stdioStatus:'complete' while dutyReceipt.status:'error' carries the invalidity signal -- which appears to be exactly the separation of concerns the schema already intends. On the evidence inspected, this looks like a moderate-value, apparently-safe improvement, but I did not drive an end-to-end test of it and it is out of scope for this package. Deviations from spec: none identified against the briefing's DoD checks. Open items: none triggered any of the 5 listed stop conditions (0 of 2 allowed failed-attempt budget used on the same problem; the launch()-selection validation issue in test B, corrected on the first attempt, was a test-authoring gap, not a stop-condition-triggering repeated failure on the production fix). No scope-boundary or ambiguity issue arose. Neither was caught until an advisor review after the implementation commit.
